# 1 Maccabees Chapter 13 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Verses:** 53 | **Disagreements:** 35

---

## Summary
The theological climax of this chapter — v.41, "the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel" — is rendered nearly identically across all four translations, reflecting its weight. Disagreements cluster around Simon's speech (vv.3-6), the ransom negotiations (vv.15-19), and the monument description (vv.27-30).

---

## Disagreements

**v.2** — "were in fear and trembling" (EMET) vs. "were trembling with fear" (LOGOS) vs. "were paralyzed with fear" (PNEUMA) vs. "were trembling with fear" (SOPHIA)

**v.3** — "You know yourselves all that I and my brothers and my father's house have done" (EMET) vs. "You know all that my brothers and I and my father's house have done" (LOGOS) — word order; LOGOS reorders to normal English syntax.
- PNEUMA: "You know what my family has given" — strongly paraphrased.

**v.4** — "have perished for the sake of Israel" (EMET) vs. "have died for Israel's sake" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "gave their lives for Israel's sake" (PNEUMA)

**v.5** — "Far be it from me to spare my life in any time of tribulation" — all four agree closely; PNEUMA: "I will not spare my own life when my people are in danger."

**v.6** — "for all the nations have gathered to destroy us out of pure hatred" — all four agree; significant phrase.

**v.7** — "the spirit of the people was rekindled" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "the spirit of the people revived" (LOGOS) vs. "put fire back into the people" (PNEUMA)

**v.12** — "wherever he turned" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "wherever he went" (LOGOS) vs. "matching him move for move" (PNEUMA) — slight variation.

**v.14** — "Jonathan had fallen into his power" (EMET) vs. "Simon had come to Jonathan's place" (LOGOS) — a significant textual difference: EMET reads ὁ Ιωναθης ἐμπεπτώκει, LOGOS reads εἰς τὸν τόπον. Context suggests LOGOS reading is correct; SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

**v.15** — "on account of the offices which he held" (EMET) vs. "on account of the offices he held" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) — minor article difference.

**v.17** — "lest he incur great hostility among the people" (EMET) vs. "lest he provoke great hostility among the people" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "because if Jonathan died and he hadn't sent them, people would blame him" (PNEUMA paraphrase)

**v.19** — "and he deceived and did not release Jonathan" (EMET) vs. "and Trypho kept his word no further and did not release Jonathan" (LOGOS) vs. "Trypho took them and freed no one" (PNEUMA) vs. "and Trypho deceived him and did not release Jonathan" (SOPHIA)

**v.20** — "went around by the road to Adora" (EMET) vs. "taking the road by way of Adora" (LOGOS) vs. "through Adora" (PNEUMA/SOPHIA)
- "kept opposite him to every place wherever he turned" (EMET) vs. "shadowed him at every turn" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.22** — "a very heavy snow" (EMET) vs. "an exceptionally heavy snowfall" (LOGOS) vs. "a massive snowstorm" (PNEUMA) vs. "a very heavy snowfall" (SOPHIA)

**v.27** — "raised it high with polished stone on the back and the front" (EMET) vs. "making it high enough to be seen; it was faced with polished stone on the front and back" (LOGOS) vs. "faced with polished stone, rising high enough to be seen from a distance" (PNEUMA) vs. "raising it high with polished stone, both front and back" (SOPHIA)

**v.28** — "for his father and his mother and his four brothers" (EMET/SOPHIA) — Note: Simon's father (Mattathias), his mother, and his four brothers: Judas, Eleazar, John, Jonathan. The seventh pyramid is presumably for Simon himself or a symbolic count.

**v.29** — "armor for a perpetual memorial" (EMET) vs. "suits of armor as an everlasting memorial" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "permanent memorial" (PNEUMA)
- "carved ships" — all agree; unique detail suggesting the prominence of maritime visibility.

**v.30** — "it stands to this day" — all four agree; authorial timestamp retained.

**v.31** — "dealt treacherously" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "dealt treacherously" (LOGOS) vs. "dealt treacherously" (PNEUMA) — rare agreement across all four.

**v.32** — "brought great evil upon the land" (EMET) vs. "brought great calamity on the land" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "his reign brought ruin on the land" (PNEUMA)

**v.33** — "walled them with high towers and great walls and gates and bars" (EMET) vs. "surrounding them with high towers and great walls, with gates and bars" (LOGOS/SOPHIA)

**v.34** — "to grant remission to the country" (EMET) vs. "to grant the country relief from taxation" (LOGOS) vs. "to lift all the burdens from the land" (PNEUMA) vs. "to grant the country relief" (SOPHIA)

**v.36** — "Friend of Kings" (all) — plural form; Simon has received this title from multiple rulers. SOPHIA capitalizes as court rank.

**v.37** — "the golden crown and the palm branch" — all agree.
- "make a complete peace" (EMET) vs. "conclude a full peace" (LOGOS) vs. "comprehensive peace" (PNEUMA) vs. "full peace" (SOPHIA)

**v.39** — "we pardon any errors and offenses" (EMET) vs. "we pardon all offenses and faults" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "we forgive all violations and infractions" (PNEUMA)
- "the crown tax which you owe" — all agree.

**v.41** — "the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel" — all four translators agree verbatim on this pivotal verse. PNEUMA converts the regnal year to "142 BCE" while others preserve regnal year.

**v.42** — "the great high priest and commander and leader of the Jews" — all agree on the full title.
- PNEUMA converts year reference to date.

**v.43** — "made an engine" (EMET) vs. "constructed a siege engine" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "brought up a siege tower" (PNEUMA — "tower" rather than "engine")

**v.45** — "give them his right hand" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "give them his right hand of peace" (LOGOS adds "of peace") vs. "show mercy" (PNEUMA loses the gesture)

**v.47** — "with hymns and blessings" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "with songs of praise and blessing" (LOGOS) vs. "to the sound of psalms and blessings" (PNEUMA)

**v.49** — "were not allowed to go out or to go into the country" (EMET) vs. "were kept from going out to the countryside" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "sealed off — no access to the country" (PNEUMA)

**v.50** — "right hand" — all preserve the surrender gesture.
- "cleansed the citadel from its pollutions" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "cleansed it from its pollutions" (LOGOS) vs. "had the citadel purified from its defilements" (PNEUMA)

**v.51** — "with praise and palm branches" (EMET) vs. "with praise and waving of palm branches" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA add "waving."
- "a great enemy had been trampled down from Israel" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "crushed and driven out of Israel" (PNEUMA)

**v.52** — "the hill of the temple which is beside the citadel" (EMET) vs. "the temple mount that stood beside the citadel" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "the temple mount adjacent to the citadel" (PNEUMA)

**v.53** — "grown up to be a man" (EMET) vs. "grown to manhood" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "grown into a man" (PNEUMA)
